about: Convert the remaining agar-agar spoon rows to grams after preferredUnit became g. Apply only after Fredrik approves. Same format as unit-decisions.json for scripts/apply-unit-decisions.mjs. No dictionary changes (agar-agar preferredUnit is already g).
sourceSnapshot: PC packs 2026-10-27 Europe/Stockholm: recipes-with-pictures 1.56.0, reversal-protocol 1.57.0, fmd-5day 1.17.0. fr-51 Coconut Mozzarella already at 7 g — not listed.

conventions.units: Write canonical unit keys (g, tsp, tbsp, pcs, ml) in all three languages; the app translates them. Do not use ts/ss/tsk/msk spellings.
conventions.ingredientChange: When change.ingredient is set, set row.ingredient to it and row.name to the dictionary names[lang] in each language; remove the old note unless change.note says otherwise (keep the existing note when change.note is absent and the ingredient is unchanged).
conventions.keepNote: When change.note is absent, keep the existing note in each language.
conventions.toTaste: change.note "to-taste": quantity null, unit "", note "to taste" (en) / "etter smak" (no) / "efter smak" (sv).
conventions.rounding: g under 20 are whole grams; spoons and pieces use quarter, third, half, two-thirds fractions only.

conversionFactors.agar-agar powder: 1 tsp ≈ 2 g, 1 tbsp ≈ 6 g (packed powder). Flakes are ~3× less potent by volume — none of these rows say flakes, and Soy Mozzarella / Coconut Mozzarella steps say powder, so powder factors are used.
